source_text: וְ/הָ/אוּלָ֡ם אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל פְּנֵ֨י הָ/אֹ֜רֶךְ עַל פְּנֵ֤י רֹֽחַב הַ/בַּ֨יִת֙ אַמּ֣וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְ/הַ/גֹּ֖בַהּ מֵאָ֣ה וְ/עֶשְׂרִ֑ים וַ/יְצַפֵּ֥/הוּ מִ/פְּנִ֖ימָה זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר־־־׃
english_snapshot: The portico that was in front of the house was twenty cubits long[a], corresponding to the width of the house, and its height was one hundred and twenty cubits; and he overlaid its interior with pure gold.

signals.text: The Hebrew text states that the portico's height was 'one hundred and twenty.' A parallel description in 1 Kings 6:3 gives the portico's length and width but not this height, and some interpreters suspect a textual difficulty here; the translation follows the Masoretic Text as preserved.

source_text: בְּ/כִכַּ֤ר הַ/יַּרְדֵּן֙ יְצָקָ֣/ם הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ בַּ/עֲבִ֖י הָ/אֲדָמָ֑ה בֵּ֥ין סֻכּ֖וֹת וּ/בֵ֥ין צְרֵדָֽתָ/ה׃
english_snapshot: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them in the clay ground[a], between Sukkoth and Zeredah.

signals.text: The parallel in 1 Kings 7:46 names the location as 'Zarethan.' Chronicles here reads 'Zeredah,' likely a variant form of the same place-name.

source_text: וְ/כִ/שְׁמֹ֨עַ אָסָ֜א הַ/דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ/אֵ֗לֶּה וְ/הַ/נְּבוּאָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד הַ/נָּבִיא֒ הִתְחַזַּ֗ק וַ/יַּעֲבֵ֤ר הַ/שִּׁקּוּצִים֙ מִ/כָּל אֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּ/בִנְיָמִ֔ן וּ/מִן הֶ֣/עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָכַ֖ד מֵ/הַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַ/יְחַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֕ר לִ/פְנֵ֖י אוּלָ֥ם יְהוָֽה־־־׃
english_snapshot: And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet[a], he took courage and removed the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities that he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed the altar of Yahweh that was before the vestibule of Yahweh.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'the prophecy of Oded the prophet.' Some interpreters and textual discussions connect this with Azariah son of Oded in the surrounding context.

source_text: וַ/יְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי מוֹאָב֩ וּ/בְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן וְ/עִמָּ/הֶ֧ם מֵֽ/הָ/עַמּוֹנִ֛ים עַל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט לַ/מִּלְחָמָֽה־׀־׃
english_snapshot: After this[a], the Moabites and the Ammonites, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'some of the Ammonites.' Many interpreters, following context and ancient versions, understand this as referring to the Meunites or a similar allied group rather than repeating the Ammonites.

source_text: וַ/יָּבֹ֨א יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט וְ/עַמּ/וֹ֮ לָ/בֹ֣ז אֶת שְׁלָלָ/ם֒ וַ/יִּמְצְאוּ֩ בָ/הֶ֨ם לָ/רֹ֜ב וּ/רְכ֤וּשׁ וּ/פְגָרִים֙ וּ/כְלֵ֣י חֲמֻד֔וֹת וַ/יְנַצְּל֥וּ לָ/הֶ֖ם לְ/אֵ֣ין מַשָּׂ֑א וַ/יִּֽהְי֞וּ יָמִ֧ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֛ה בֹּזְזִ֥ים אֶת הַ/שָּׁלָ֖ל כִּ֥י רַב הֽוּא־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil[a], and they found among them in abundance goods, garments, and desirable articles; and they took for themselves more than they could carry. They were three days plundering the spoil, because it was so much.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'corpses.' Some ancient witnesses and translations reflect a reading such as 'garments' or omit the term to smooth the sense of the inventory, but the Masoretic Text reads 'corpses,' likely indicating the fallen enemy bodies among whom the spoil was found.

source_text: בֶּן אַרְבָּעִ֨ים וּ/שְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בְ/מָלְכ֔/וֹ וְ/שָׁנָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽ/ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ/שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔/וֹ עֲתַלְיָ֖הוּ בַּת עָמְרִֽי־־׃
english_snapshot: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king[a], and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah[b], the daughter of Omri.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'forty-two years old.' The parallel in 2 Kgs 8:26 reads 'twenty-two years old,' so some understand this as a textual problem or propose another way of reckoning the number.

source_text: וַ/עֲתַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֵ֣ם אֲחַזְיָ֔הוּ רָאֲתָ֖ה כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת בְּנָ֑/הּ וַ/תָּ֗קָם וַ/תְּדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת כָּל זֶ֥רַע הַ/מַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְ/בֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה־־׃
english_snapshot: Athaliah[a], the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, and she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring of the house of Judah.

signals.text: Hebrew has a difficult verb form here, literally 'spoke,' but the context and the parallel in 2 Kings 11:1 support the sense 'destroyed' or 'put to death.'

source_text: וַ/יְהִי֙ לִ/דְרֹ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֔ים בִּ/ימֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֔הוּ הַ/מֵּבִ֖ין בִּ/רְאֹ֣ת הָ/אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּ/בִ/ימֵי֙ דָּרְשׁ֣/וֹ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה הִצְלִיח֖/וֹ הָ/אֱלֹהִֽים־׃ס
english_snapshot: He continued to seek God in the days of Zechariah[a], who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought Yahweh[b], God made him prosper.

signals.text: Or, 'who instructed in the fear of God.' The Hebrew phrase is difficult; the Masoretic Text more literally reads 'who had understanding in the visions of God.'

source_text: וְ/עַצְמוֹת֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים שָׂרַ֖ף עַל מזבחותים וַ/יְטַהֵ֥ר אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה וְ/אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם־־־׃
english_snapshot: He burned the bones of the priests on their altars[a], and he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.

signals.text: Or 'the altars.' The Hebrew form here is unusual; the sense is that Josiah burned the priests' bones on the altars associated with them.

source_text: וּ/בְ/עָרֵ֨י מְנַשֶּׁ֧ה וְ/אֶפְרַ֛יִם וְ/שִׁמְע֖וֹן וְ/עַד נַפְתָּלִ֑י ב/הר בתי/הם סָבִֽיב־׃
english_snapshot: and in the cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon[a], even as far as Naphtali[b], in their surrounding ruins.

signals.text: Hebrew text is difficult in the final phrase; literally, something like 'in/with their ... סביב.' Many translations understand the sense to be 'in their surrounding ruins/desolate places.'

source_text: וַ/יְצַ֣ו הַ/מֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת חִלְקִיָּ֡הוּ וְ/אֶת אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן שָׁ֠פָן וְ/אֶת עַבְדּ֨וֹן בֶּן מִיכָ֜ה וְ/אֵ֣ת שָׁפָ֣ן הַ/סּוֹפֵ֗ר וְ/אֵ֛ת עֲשָׂיָ֥ה עֶֽבֶד הַ/מֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵ/אמֹֽר־־־־־׀־׃
english_snapshot: Then the king commanded Hilkiah[a], Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying[b],

signals.text: The Masoretic Text reads 'Abdon son of Micah.' The parallel in 2 Kings 22:12 has 'Achbor son of Micaiah.'

source_text: בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנִים֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּ/מָלְכ֔/וֹ וּ/שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַ/עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ/ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַ/יַּ֥עַשׂ הָ/רַ֖ע בְּ/עֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה־׃
english_snapshot: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign[a], and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the sight of Yahweh.

signals.text: 2 Kings 24:8 reads 'eighteen years old' instead of 'eight years old.'
